football_evidence.question: Can Arkansas State’s pass rush get to Landry Lyddy?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Southern Miss, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.5 of the 4.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Southern Miss has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Southern Miss’ offense has allowed a sack on 5.2% of its dropbacks, and Arkansas State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 2.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Southern Miss has the ball (big plays through the air): Southern Miss’ offense turns 13.1% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Arkansas State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 14.1% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When Southern Miss has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Southern Miss’ offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.0% of its runs, and Arkansas State’s defense stops 10.6% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Southern Miss has the ball (the red zone): Southern Miss’ offense succeeds on 39.8% of its red-zone plays, and Arkansas State’s defense allows success on 54.8% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.8%).
contradicting: When Arkansas State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Arkansas State’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.5% of its dropbacks, and Southern Miss’ defense sacks the quarterback on 2.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Arkansas State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Arkansas State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 13.5% of its runs, and Southern Miss’ defense stops 12.3% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Southern Miss has the ball (big plays on the ground): Southern Miss’ offense turns 4.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Arkansas State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Arkansas State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Arkansas State’s offense averages 8.5 yards per pass attempt, and Southern Miss’ defense allows 8.0 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
quarterbacks: Landry Lyddy has completed 62 of 100 passes (62.0%) for 824 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for Southern Miss, and has been sacked on 9 of 109 dropbacks.
